subsystems.name: Graphene oxide feedstock
subsystems.role: supplies the single-atom-thick sheets that become the building blocks of the framework.

subsystems.name: Gel network
subsystems.role: links the sheets into a free-standing three-dimensional network instead of letting them restack.

subsystems.name: Pore template
subsystems.role: decides how big and how aligned the pores end up.

subsystems.name: Drying stage
subsystems.role: removes the frozen solvent without liquid surface tension crushing the pores.

subsystems.name: Reduction stage
subsystems.role: strips oxygen groups off the sheets and restores electrical conductivity.

subsystems.name: Functionalisation and forming
subsystems.role: tailors the surface chemistry and shapes the material for its application.

buildSteps.title: Make graphene oxide
buildSteps.detail: Graphite flakes are oxidised in acid with strong oxidants, then washed and dispersed in water, where the layers separate into single sheets, typically a fraction of a micrometre across.

buildSteps.title: Form a suspension
buildSteps.detail: The sheets are dispersed in water at a chosen concentration; binders, crosslinkers or a second phase such as a polymer or metal salt may be added.

buildSteps.title: Gel the network
buildSteps.detail: Heating under pressure, or adding a crosslinker, makes the sheets join edge-to-face and face-to-face into a wet hydrogel that holds its shape.

buildSteps.title: Shape the part
buildSteps.detail: The hydrogel is cast into a mould, drawn into a film, or broken into granules, depending on the final product.

buildSteps.title: Freeze and template the pores
buildSteps.detail: Controlled freezing grows ice crystals through the gel; the crystals push the sheets aside, so their size and direction become the pores of the finished material.

buildSteps.title: Freeze-dry
buildSteps.detail: Under vacuum the ice sublimes straight to vapour, leaving a sponge of graphene sheets that would otherwise collapse if simply air-dried.

buildSteps.title: Reduce and anneal
buildSteps.detail: The sponge is heated in an inert atmosphere, often to several hundred degrees Celsius or more, to remove oxygen groups and partially restore the graphene lattice.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise and finish
buildSteps.detail: Dopants, metal oxides or catalysts are added, then the material is washed, dried, cut or pressed, and tested for density, pore size, surface area and conductivity.

prerequisites.tech: Graphene oxide production at industrial scale
prerequisites.why: quantities are growing but cost, batch consistency and sheet quality still limit commercial use.
lyophilisation is mature in food and pharma, but scaling it to uniform metre-scale blocks is not routine.
furnaces of this kind are standard in metallurgy and carbon manufacturing.
gas adsorption, mercury porosimetry and electron microscopy are needed to prove pore structure and surface area.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap routes to strong, low-density monoliths
prerequisites.why: many laboratory aerogels are mechanically fragile, which limits insulation, filtration and capture uses.

pathway.milestone: gram- to kilogram-scale aerogels demonstrated in laboratories and pilot plants
pathway.unlocks: electrodes, absorbents and sensor materials where high surface area matters more than low cost.

pathway.milestone: repeatable, low-cost production of uniform monoliths and granules
pathway.unlocks: filtration membranes, carbon-capture sorbents and oil-spill absorbents.

pathway.milestone: robust composites in which the aerogel is the filler or the skeleton
pathway.unlocks: thermal insulation and lightweight structural parts.

pathway.milestone: use in industrial gas separation and capture plants
pathway.unlocks: lower-energy capture of carbon dioxide from flue gas or air, if the material survives thousands of cycles.
